- If sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent days, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to align with bullish momentum.  
- If model shows gradual, flat upward trend (e.g., +0.1–0.2 per day) but true outcome spikes sharply, adjust forecast to allow for acceleration or overshoot after initial lag.  
- When true outcome exceeds model by >5% over 3–5 days, consider mean reversion bias — reduce forecast slope slightly to avoid overestimating continuation.  
- If sentiment is neutral or negative (≤0.1) and model is rising steadily, check for lag — true outcome often exceeds model by 2–4% in early days of trend.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if model is flat or slightly rising but true outcome shows strong upward momentum, apply a “spike correction” — add 1–2% per day to forecast after 10–15 days of low volatility.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.33 spikes (e.g., 2023-01-25, 2023-01-27), model tends to undercorrect — forecast should be 2–3% higher than model to account for sentiment-driven overreaction.  
- Avoid overfitting to recent history — if model is forecasting based on last 3–5 days and true outcome diverges, reduce forecast sensitivity to recent data.
